policy: Research-created structured comparison of Steiner's conceptual schemes. No source text is reproduced. All claims are attributed to the linked original work and remain subject to translation/context review.

models.title: Steiner's layered worldview framework (GA 151)
models.status: located + scheme compared with original lecture, translation not collated
models.summary: Steiner describes not one flat taxonomy but twelve worldview orientations, seven ways of holding or approaching them, three possible tones, and anthropomorphism as a special case. His zodiacal and planetary correspondences are part of his spiritual-cosmological account, not an accepted astronomical or psychological classification.

sections.title: Twelve orientations and their symbolic zodiacal correspondences
Seven worldview moods and their symbolic planetary correspondences
Three tones and the special case
rows: Earth regarded on its own (special case)

distinctions: Orientation and mood are not synonyms: in Steiner's analogy a worldview mood may occur with different orientations.
Three tones modify the resulting worldview; anthropomorphism is treated as a separate case.
12 + 7 + 3 + 1 = 23 named conceptual positions in this lecture; this is not a count of mutually exclusive complete philosophies.
The zodiac/planet parallels are Steiner's asserted spiritual analogies and not validated empirical correspondences.

models.title: Ninefold and sevenfold accounts of the human being (GA 9)
models.status: located + schema compared with original chapter; translation variants not collated
models.summary: In Theosophy, Steiner presents body, soul and spirit as different aspects of the human being, lists nine members, and then explains a condensed sevenfold presentation in the earthly person. These are related but not interchangeable with the later physiological threefold organization of nerve-sense, rhythmic and metabolic-limb activities.

sections.title: Sevenfold condensation
rows: Sentient soul body (soul body + sentient soul)
Spirit-filled consciousness soul (consciousness soul + spirit self)

distinctions: The earthly sevenfold account combines the ninefold items 3–4 and items 6–7 as paired unities; do not arbitrarily discard other members.
Fourfold human constitution (physical, etheric, astral, I) is another classification context and should be studied without conflating it with the ninefold enumeration.
The threefold physiological organization discussed in education and medicine is a separate schema; cross-link rather than merge these branches.
Terms and enumerations can differ across translations and lecture contexts; maintain exact work/edition metadata.

models.title: Distinguishing bodily organization from the ninefold schema
models.summary: In the education lecture of 5 September 1919, Steiner contrasts the head, chest or trunk, and limb organization of the human bodily form. It should not be mistaken for the physical/etheric/astral members in the fourfold body organization or the ninefold and sevenfold schemas of Theosophy.
distinctions: Do not place 'physical body, etheric body, astral body' as an equivalent list of head, rhythmic/chest, metabolic-limb organization.
Further compare the educational presentation with original medical lectures before asserting a complete one-to-one correspondence.
